questions.explain: Engineers don't ignore costs from carelessness — costs are invisible at the point where decisions are made (a staging instance provisioned at 11 PM Tuesday isn't evaluated as $1.008/hr × 720), and Finance notices 30–45 days later, when the action-cost connection has evaporated. Fix: push cost data to the decision point via tags, engineer-facing surfaces, and a fast feedback loop.
options: Costs are invisible where decisions are made and Finance notices 30–45 days later — fix by tagging, surfacing costs in engineer tools (Grafana/Datadog/terminal), and making the feedback loop fast
questions.q: Why don't engineers care about database costs today, and what is the structural fix?

questions.explain: Showing a team's monthly bill is useful; showing which queries generate it is transformative — when an engineer sees their unindexed join costs $400/month, they fix it next sprint because the number is attached to code they wrote. Use Query Store/dm_exec_query_stats with a calibrated vCPU-hour rate to rank queries by estimated monthly cost.
options: Show which specific queries generate the bill — e.g., an unindexed join at $400/month gets fixed because the number attaches to code the engineer wrote
questions.q: Why is query-level cost attribution transformative for engineering behavior?

questions.explain: Set the initial budget at the team's trailing 3-month average spend + 15% growth headroom, rounded to the nearest $500 — month one must feel credible, not an emergency; after 2–3 months of trusted data, tighten 10% per quarter toward steady state. Escalation: 70% informational Slack, 85% alert + lead, 100% required review meeting, 120% automatic PR comment estimating the new instance's monthly cost.
options: Initial budget = trailing 3-month avg + 15% headroom (rounded to $500); tighten 10%/quarter after trust; escalate 70%/85%/100%/120% with a PR cost-comment at 120%
Budgets should be identical for all teams
questions.q: How should per-team database budgets be set, tuned, and escalated?

questions.explain: Three patterns: (1) Infracost in CI annotating Terraform plans with cost deltas before merge ('Monthly cost will increase by $481.14 (+91%)' in the PR); (2) weekly cost digest with anomaly detection to Slack every Monday; (3) non-production shutdown enforcement via opt-in auto-shutdown=enabled tag — staging db.r6g.2xlarge drops $530→$180/mo on business-hours schedule, $350/mo per instance ($42k/yr for 10).
options: Infracost cost deltas in CI PRs, weekly anomaly digest to Slack, and opt-in non-prod shutdown (staging 2xlarge $530→$180/mo = $350/mo per instance)
questions.q: What three automation patterns embed cost signals into the engineering workflow?

questions.explain: Make cost a first-class engineering metric alongside latency, error rate, and uptime — never penalize spending itself, which creates wrong incentives (teams under-provision and cause incidents). The accountability mechanism is per-team budgets with automated alerting, with the message going to the team's engineering channel — the people who can act on it.
options: Accountability means penalizing spend; make cost a first-class metric alongside latency/error rate/uptime without penalizing spending, and alert the team's engineering channel
questions.q: How do you create cost accountability without creating friction?

title: FinOps Culture: Getting Engineers to Care About Database Costs
